meta.title: Trump Tariff Escalation Thesis — March 2026
meta.claim: Tariff shock transmits through input costs → retail prices → consumer confidence → employment (Layer 2) and retaliation → agriculture → rural economy (Layer 3). The Section 122 expiration on July 24 is the pivot date. Trade the policy uncertainty, not the tariffs themselves.

nodes.label: Tariff Escalation
nodes.context: Supreme Court struck down IEEPA tariffs 6-3 on Feb 20. Trump pivoted same day to Section 122 (10% global, 150-day limit). Bessent says 15% coming. China at 34% via Section 301. Autos 25% (15% for Japan/EU via deals). Semiconductors 25% on advanced chips. Effective avg rate 13.7% — highest since Smoot-Hawley.

tvAlertBindings.description: Pine alert on SPY close below the 200-day SMA for the first time in 60 days. Webhook body must carry 'value' with the new probability (typically 0.95 for tariff escalation confirmation). Technical market confirmation of the macro thesis.

nodes.label: Input Cost Surge
nodes.context: PPI goods inflation at 5.8% annualized. Tariffs add 70+ bps to core inflation per Goldman. Firms with weak pricing power face margin compression. Import costs for steel up 41%, autos up 25%.

nodes.label: Supply Chain Disruption
nodes.context: Companies restructuring supply chains around tariff walls. Semiconductor advanced chips face 25% tariff. China shifting soybean purchases from US to Brazil permanently. Value chain fragmentation increasing costs across all sectors.

nodes.label: Auto Sector Stress
nodes.context: 25% Section 232 auto tariff since April 2025 (reduced to 15% for Japan/EU via deals). Average new vehicle price impact $2,500-4,000. Automakers absorbing partial costs via margin compression. Detroit Three all guiding lower for 2026.

nodes.label: Tech/Semiconductor Stress
nodes.context: Jan 2026: 25% Section 232 tariff on advanced semiconductor imports (Nvidia H200, AMD MI325X). Broader China chip tariffs deferred to 2027 under Trump-Xi truce. Export licensing requirements tightened. US-China tech decoupling accelerating.

nodes.label: Consumer Price Transmission
nodes.context: Core PCE at 2.7% (Fed March projection, revised up). Tariffs added 1.3pp to core goods inflation. Year-ahead inflation expectations jumped to 3.8% in March (UMich). Feb CPI showed receding goods costs but rising services. The pass-through is happening — $1,500/household average tax increase.

nodes.label: Agricultural Retaliation
nodes.context: China retaliated with tariffs up to 125% on US goods in 2025, now at 10% under 90-day truce. But the damage is structural: China shifted 80% of soybean imports to Brazil/Argentina (from 60% pre-trade-war). US farmers permanently losing key markets. 2026 growing season planning disrupted by tariff uncertainty.

nodes.label: USD/CNY Stress
nodes.context: USD/CNY at 6.916 — yuan has actually strengthened 4.8% over 12 months. China using currency stability as a policy tool, not weaponizing it. But if tariffs escalate further or truce breaks, PBOC may allow managed depreciation to offset tariff impact. 7.00 is the key level.

nodes.label: Consumer Confidence Collapse
nodes.context: UMich consumer sentiment at 53.3 — lowest of 2026, lowest annual avg in 70+ year survey history. Year-ahead inflation expectations surged to 3.8%. 70% of Americans predicting economic difficulty in 2026. Triple hit: tariff price increases + oil shock + geopolitical anxiety.

nodes.label: Manufacturing PMI

feeds.label: ISM Mfg PMI (FRED dropped NAPM on licensing — 400s; type it in)

nodes.context: ISM Manufacturing PMI at 52.4 in Feb — second straight expansion, but only 3rd in 40 months. Manufacturing briefly recovering from tariff-induced restocking, but the bounce is fragile. Services PMI flash dipped below 50 in Feb for first time in 2 years. March data due April 1.

nodes.label: Section 122 Expiration
nodes.context: Section 122 tariffs expire after 150 days on July 24, 2026. Extension requires Congressional approval. This is the binary pivot: either Congress extends (escalation), tariffs lapse (de-escalation), or Trump finds another legal authority. Bessent says rates return to prior levels within 5 months.

nodes.label: Earnings Compression
nodes.context: S&P 500 at 6,370, pulled back 6.4% from 6,800 highs. Tariff uncertainty widening dispersion — firms with weak pricing power face margin compression, aggressive passthrough risks slower sales. Q1 earnings season (April) will reveal tariff damage. Small caps (IWM) initially outperformed on domestic-revenue thesis but re-rating.

nodes.label: Fed Policy Response
nodes.context: Fed held at 3.50-3.75% in March (11-1 vote). Dot plot shows 1 cut in 2026, 1 in 2027. Powell framing tariffs as 'one-time price effects' — but oil shock complicates. Goldman pushed expected cuts to Sept/Dec. Fed trapped: inflation above target but growth slowing = stagflation risk. Next decision May 6-7.

nodes.label: Trade Deal / De-escalation
nodes.additionalCondition: Announced tariff reduction or bilateral deal
nodes.action: Unwind hedges (SH, TLT overweight), add XLY/IWM, reduce DBA/GLD
nodes.context: Polymarket: 71% Trump visits China by June 30. Section 122 expires July 24 unless Congress extends. ~20 bilateral deals already negotiated. IEEPA refund question ($200B+) still pending. De-escalation is the base case but timing uncertain.

nodes.label: Recession Risk
nodes.context: Polymarket: 38% recession by end-2026. Goldman: 25% (raised from baseline after Feb jobs + oil). JPM: 'no recession but material headwinds.' Bloomberg consensus: 1.5% GDP growth. The tariff tax ($1,500/household) + oil shock + geopolitical uncertainty create a triple drag. Stagflation — inflation above target with slowing growth — is the central risk.

nodes.label: Tariff Escalation Rhetoric (GDELT)
nodes.context: Live GDELT article-volume for tariff escalation coverage (query: "tariff" AND China/Section 122/IEEPA, English). Watch-only news pulse (no causal edge by design): declaring the feed here is what lights up the desk's bridge news endpoint, so Dialectic's get_thesis_news tool gets real headlines for this book instead of 'no gdelt config'. Rhetoric spiking while USD/CNY and input costs stay flat = political noise; rhetoric plus market confirmation = escalation transmitting.

scenarios.name: Trade deal before Section 122 expiry
scenarios.notes: Trump visits China (71% by June per Polymarket), strikes bilateral deal. Section 122 lapses on July 24. Effective tariffs drop to 5-8% (Section 301 baseline). Market relief rally. Consumer confidence recovers.

scenarios.name: Congress extends Section 122 tariffs
scenarios.notes: Congress votes to extend tariffs past July 24. Effective rate stays at 13-15%. Uncertainty becomes permanence. Corporate investment freezes. Earnings revisions accelerate downward.

scenarios.name: Tariff escalation — new authority or higher rates
scenarios.notes: Trump finds new legal authority after Section 122 expires, or Congress grants broad tariff powers. Rates increase to 20-25% global, 50%+ on China. Full trade war. Yuan breaks 7.20. Recession probability spikes.

scenarios.name: Stagflation materializes
scenarios.notes: Worst case: tariff inflation + oil shock + slowing growth = stagflation. Core PCE above 3%, GDP below 1%. Fed trapped — cutting fuels inflation, holding kills growth. 1970s analog.

scenarios.name: Muddle through — tariffs fade, economy absorbs
scenarios.notes: Tariffs stay but don't escalate. Economy absorbs the shock. Growth slows to 1.5% but avoids recession. Inflation drifts down as one-time effects pass through. Markets chop sideways.

analogs.name: Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act (1930)
lessons: Retaliation is automatic and escalatory — 24 countries responded within 2 years.
Global trade collapsed 65% — the tariffs deepened the Depression, they didn't cause it.
Both episodes started during expansion (1929 growth, 2024-25 growth), not recession.
Agricultural exporters were the hardest hit — farm income collapsed.
The political feedback loop delayed repeal by 4 years despite obvious damage.
analogs.notes: Structural analog: broad tariff increase during expansion, met with retaliation, deepening existing stress. The 2026 effective tariff rate (13.7%) is the highest since Smoot-Hawley. Key difference: modern economy is services-heavy and supply-chain-integrated.

analogs.name: 2018-2019 US-China Trade War
lessons: China's retaliatory tariffs permanently shifted soybean sourcing to Brazil.
Market sell-off forced Fed pivot from hiking to cutting within 7 months.
Small caps initially outperformed on domestic revenue thesis — then underperformed.
Phase 1 deal ($200B purchase commitments) was never fully implemented.
The $28B farm bailout exceeded the entire 2009 auto bailout.
analogs.notes: Most direct analog. S&P fell 19.8%, soybeans -18%, CNY weakened to 7.18. Fed pivoted. Farm bailout $28B. Key difference: 2026 tariffs broader (Section 122 is global) and higher effective rate. Oil shock simultaneous this time.

analogs.name: Nixon Import Surcharge (1971)
lessons: 10% import surcharge was temporary (4 months) and used as negotiating leverage.
Section 122 has the same 150-day statutory limit — same playbook.
The surcharge worked: Smithsonian Agreement within 4 months.
Inflationary effects of the broader Nixon Shock took years to materialize.
Gold was the ultimate winner of the policy regime change.
analogs.notes: Closest legal analog: Nixon used a 10% import surcharge as leverage, removed it in 4 months via Smithsonian Agreement. Trump's Section 122 has the same 150-day limit and similar leverage logic.

rules: Review 2x/week: Tuesday close, Friday close. Friday = end-of-week macro data.
Never deploy > 1/3 SGOV on one signal. Budget: $800/month reserve.
No single position > 12% of total book. Overlays max 5% each.
Section 122 is the pivot: July 24 expiration is the single most important date. Position for both outcomes.
Don't front-run the deal: Polymarket says 71% Trump visits China by June. That's priced in. Wait for confirmed policy change.
Earnings season discipline: Q1 reports (April) will reveal tariff damage. Don't add to losers before the data.
Retaliation asymmetry: US tariffs hurt importers (consumers); retaliation hurts exporters (farmers). Different instruments for different channels.
Graph propagation: When upstream node fires, check all downstream edges. Estimated lags are planning windows, not execution triggers.
Confluence rule: consumer-confidence and earnings-compression are the primary confluence nodes. 3+ fired upstream edges = highest conviction.
Analog calibration: Use 2018 trade war lags as planning baseline. PMI contraction within 6 months, market bottom at 9 months, deal at 21 months.
Stagflation hedge: If core PCE > 3.0% AND GDP < 1.0%, activate stagflation overlay immediately. GLD + GDX + TIPS.

provenance.methodology: Causal DAG with expert-specified transmission mechanisms, lags, and strengths. The tariff thesis models two distinct transmission channels: (1) cost pass-through (input costs → retail prices → consumer confidence → earnings → recession risk) and (2) retaliation (tariffs → Chinese retaliatory tariffs → agricultural market loss → rural economy). Edge strengths are subjective conditional probabilities calibrated against 2018-2019 trade war data. Scenarios are probability-weighted with portfolioimpacts estimated via factor betas. Cascade phases use checklist-based signpost tracking.
limitations: Section 122 legal challenge risk not modeled — courts could strike it down too.
IEEPA tariff refund ($200B+) resolution timing uncertain — could create market shock.
China's policy response (managed depreciation, rare earth restrictions) only partially modeled.
Tariff pass-through elasticities vary widely by product — uniform estimates are imprecise.
Manufacturing PMI restocking bounce may mask underlying weakness — 2 months is not a trend.
Polymarket probabilities may not reflect informed views on Congressional vote dynamics.
Oil shock (Iran/Hormuz) is running simultaneously — difficult to isolate tariff effects.
Edge strengths are expert estimates calibrated against 2018 analog, not empirically derived.
Monthly rebalancing assumed — actual execution may differ.
provenance.disclaimer: Research framework for structured expert judgment, not financial advice. All instruments carry risk of loss. The math enforces consistency — it does not generate predictions. This thesis runs alongside the Iran/Hormuz thesis — cross-effects (oil + tariffs = stagflation) are partially modeled through the consumer confidence and recession risk confluence nodes.
